title: The strong Atiyah conjecture and von Neumann ranks for graphs of groups with finite-index edge inclusions
description: Let G be the fundamental group of a graph of groups in which each edge group has finite index in both incident vertex groups. If the von Neumann matrix ranks at each vertex generate a discrete subgroup of the real numbers, we prove that the rank group of G is exactly the sum of the vertex rank groups. This gives permanence for the strong Atiyah conjecture with bounded torsion. The proof expresses a rank as a minimum over edge projections and shows that modules over the edge regular closures attain it simultaneously. In the torsion-free case with integral vertex ranks, the affiliated division ring is the universal field of the graph of vertex division rings. For finite graphs of finitely generated free groups, rational matrix ranks are computable. Applications include finitely presented infinite simple groups acting on products of trees and the exact conjectured denominator for every subgroup of GL₂(ℚ). In SL₂(ℤ[1/2]) an integral group-ring element has kernel dimension 1/12, although every torsion-free subgroup of finite index has index divisible by 24.
notes: Preprint. Version 2.0.0, a major revision with a new title: the organizing result is now a rank theorem for graphs of groups with finite-index edge inclusions and bounded torsion, which subsumes the amalgam theorem of version 1.0.0.
